questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Composition of the Atmosphere' refers to.
questions.a: The atmosphere is a blanket of mixed gases - nitrogen the largest share, oxygen vital for breathing, carbon dioxide small but heat-trapping - along with water vapour and dust; each component plays a role in weather, climate and life.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Composition of the Atmosphere'.
questions.a: Nitrogen dominates, oxygen sustains, carbon dioxide warms: every gas has a job.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Composition of the Atmosphere' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3 (source: iest103.txt opening sections (composition of the atmosphere))

concepts.title: Weather and Climate: Elements and Difference

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Weather and Climate: Elements and Difference' refers to.
questions.a: Weather is the hour-to-hour state of temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, cloud and rainfall, while climate is the long-term average pattern of weather of a place; the two share elements but differ in timescale.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Weather and Climate: Elements and Difference'.
questions.a: Weather is today's mood, climate is long-term character.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Weather and Climate: Elements and Difference' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3 (source: iest103.txt sections on weather, climate and their elements)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Climate Change and Its Impacts' refers to.
questions.a: Human activities raise greenhouse gases and warm the planet, shifting rainfall patterns, melting glaciers and raising seas; understanding the atmosphere helps citizens read these changes and support mitigation and adaptation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Climate Change and Its Impacts'.
questions.a: The blanket is thickening: climate change rewrites weather patterns worldwide.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Climate Change and Its Impacts' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3 (source: iest103.txt sections on climate change and impacts)
